title: 'Please Put Them On, Takamine-san' Manga Ends in January
content:
The December issue of Gangan Joker published a new chapter on Friday, but Square Enix will not publish a new chapter in the January 2027 issue in December.

Hiiragi ( Kakegurui Midari ) launched the manga in Gangan Joker in January 2019. Square Enix published the manga's 11th volume on February 20.

Yen Press is releasing the manga in English, and describes the story:

Takane Takamine is the goddess of her high school. With perfect grades, athletic prowess, and unrivaled beauty, this student council president is the apple of everyone's eye-including Koushi Shirota, a below-average student with no friends or social prospects whatsoever. But he'll soon find out the secret behind Takamine's unbelievable success-her underwear! When she strips, she can undo any of her past actions, and now that Koushi knows, Takamine won't let him off so easy...

Yen Press published the manga's 10th volume in English on February 24.

The manga's television anime adaptation debuted in April 2025. Crunchyroll streamed the series as it aired.

title: Suu Morishita's A Sign of Affection Manga Ends in 3 Chapters
content:
Morishita revealed January that the manga is heading toward its climax.

Kodansha had revealed in May the manga has exceeded 7.8 million copies in circulation worldwide.

Kodansha USA Publishing and Kodansha 's K MANGA service both publish the manga in English digitally. Kodansha USA describes the manga:

Yuki is a typical college student, whose world revolves around her friends, social media, and the latest sales. But when a chance encounter on a train leads to her meeting friend-of-a-friend and fellow student Itsuomi-san, her world starts to widen. But even though Itsuomi-kun can speak three languages, sign language isn't one of them. Can the two learn to communicate the budding feelings between them?

Morishita launched the manga in Kodansha 's Dessert magazine in July 2019. Kodansha published the manga's 14th compiled book volume on May 13, and will publish the 15th volume on December 11.

The manga's anime adaptation debuted in January 2024. Crunchyroll streamed the series as it aired and also streams an English dub.

title: Manga 'Yubisaki to Renren' Ends in Three Chapters
content:
The official X (formerly Twitter) account of Dessert magazine announced on Saturday that Suu Morishita 's Yubisaki to Renren ( A Sign of Affection ) manga will end in three chapters. The 63rd chapter will mark the manga's conclusion.

Morishita began serializing the romance manga in Dessert magazine in July 2019. The manga went on hiatus in June 2021 due to Morishita giving birth, and resumed serialization in November of the same year. Kodansha published the 14th volume on May 13, with the 15th volume scheduled for a December 11 release. The manga has a cumulative 7.5 million copies of its volumes in circulation.

Kodansha USA licensed the manga in English in March 2020. The 12th volume was released digitally in December 2025.

Yubisaki to Renren received the Grand Prize at the 11th An An Manga Award in 2020 and ranked 17th in the Comics category at the 2020 Tsugi ni Kuru Manga Taisho . The manga also ranked ninth and 17th in the Women's category of Takarajimasha's Kono Manga ga Sugoi! rankings in 2021 and 2022 , respectively, and placed first in the Women's category of BookLive's Annual Bookstore Staff Suzuki Award in 2021. It was nominated for the Kodansha Manga Award in the Shoujo category four consecutive times from 2021 , 2022 , 2023 , and 2024 . The manga also received awards at the 1st and 2nd Minna no Oshi Renai Manga Taisho in 2022 and 2023 , respectively.

A 12-episode television anime adaptation produced by Ajia-do aired in Winter 2024. Crunchyroll simulcast the anime with subtitles in multiple languages and an English dub.

Official manga site: https://go-dessert.jp/c/renren.html

title: One Piece’s Elbaph Arc Teases Luffy Is One Step Closer to Gear 6
content:
Warning: This article contains spoilers from the One Piece manga! Luffy’s powers continue to grow in the ongoing Elbaph Arc. It’s been over two years since One Piece entered the second arc of the Final Saga, and the situation hasn’t been worse than this. It didn’t take long for Elbaph to turn into a battlefield when the Holy Knights arrived there with the intention of making them bend to Imu’s will. The World Government has been eyeing the power of the strongest race, and they don’t plan on waiting longer now that the war is upon them. After seeing that the Holy Knights may not be able to accomplish their goals, Imu descended on the island and finally revealed his true appearance.

The mysterious ruler of the world is even more powerful than fans imagined, which just proves the gap in power between him and Luffy. Luffy has been on a whole other level ever since he awakened his Devil Fruit in Wano. His Gear 5 comes with incredible powers , but the drawbacks make it impossible for him to defeat powerful opponents effortlessly. However, as the fight against Imu continues, Luffy taps into his mysterious powers that may hint at his true awakening or his Gear 6 form.

Luffy Might Unlock Gear 6 in One Piece

For some time, fans believed that Gear 5 is truly the peak of his powers because of what he said in Wano during his awakening. Luffy never felt this powerful before, which is all the more reason why he called his awakening his “peak.” Luffy managed to overpower Kaido and save Wano, but that was only the beginning. The series introduced the limitations related to Gear 5, and the Egghead Island Arc made it clear that Luffy isn’t powerful enough to defeat the major villains.

Things became even worse in Elbaph when Imu effortlessly stabbed him even when he was in his Gear 5 form. This near-death situation again caused Luffy to tap into a new level of power. Luffy awakened his Gear 5 in a similar way after he was fatally injured in Wano. However, this time, instead of another awakening, Luffy revealed a new form that shifts into a more feral, monkey-like state that giants refer to as Dark Nika in motifs. The series hasn’t officially dubbed this form as Gear 6, and the true abilities of Luffy in this form are still unknown.

However, this is most likely the first step towards him unlocking the true potential of his Devil Fruit. After meeting Luffy, Imu knew that he was nowhere near the level of Joyboy, which was yet another hint that the young pirate hasn’t unlocked all his powers yet. Luffy’s Devil Fruit is as mysterious as it is whimsical. It allows him to turn imagination into reality and transform into something of a mythical being. Even so, without truly understanding his own powers, he will never be able to defeat the big shots, especially Imu.

Luffy’s New Power Up Needs to Overcome The Biggest Drawback of Gear 5

The reason why Luffy achieving a Gear 6 is more crucial than ever is because of the drawbacks of his Gear 5 form. While combining his Devil Fruit powers with Haki, his stamina drains instantly, something the series already revealed in Dressrosa when his Gear 4 form was introduced. However, this problem became even more evident with his Gear 5, especially since whenever Luffy drains his stamina, he starts looking like an old man who can’t even lift a finger. The only way he can get back into fighting is by filling his stomach and getting his energy back, which takes time.

The battles are already intense, and it gets even more impossible for others to buy him enough time to replenish his energy. This happened to him several times in Egghead, and he keeps running into the same problem all over again. At this rate, his Gear 5 form is only good enough to defeat opponents like Rob Lucci or anyone weak enough so Luffy can deal with them in just a few blows. However, when faced against the Five Elders, Holy Knights, and even Imu, Luffy needs much more power than he realizes.

Do you think One Piece is setting up the stage for Luffy’s Gear 6? What kind of powers do you think he can unlock next? Share your thoughts in the comments below.

title: 3 Things We Need to See in Avatar: Seven Havens Season 2
content:
Avatar: Seven Havens wrapped up its first season at the end of last month, leaving behind several burning questions. This is the first animation series of the franchise in 12 years, and there’s no doubt the wait was worth it. The latest installment earned praise from fans and critics for its exceptional worldbuilding and captivating characters. The series premiered in October and ended in the same month after releasing the episodes in batches. The story centers around twin Earthbender sisters, Pavi and Nisha, as they navigate a world where the Avatar is feared among the masses rather than being treated as a savior.

The finale of Book 1 features Pavi heading off to the next Haven while Nisha decides to stay behind in Allora with Karthik. This helps the franchise set up the overarching journey for the upcoming seasons, which means fans are in for a new adventure. There are still a lot of things the story needs to resolve in the second season, but so far, there hasn’t been much information on the story. This is especially the case since the series hasn’t yet revealed a trailer or even a teaser. Regardless, here are three things we have to see in Avatar: Seven Havens Season 2 .

3) Korra’s Fate Is Still a Mystery

Since the story takes place 225 years after The Legend of Korra , it’s evident she is dead in Seven Havens, but the exact circumstances of her death haven’t been revealed yet. Since humanity blames Korra for the cataclysm, Avatars are now feared in the world because of the terrifying abilities they possess. The first season only began to scratch the surface of what led her to destroy the world with the cataclysm.

Less than a week ago, executive producer Sehaj Sethi took part in a Reddit AMA and answered all sorts of fan questions about the upcoming season. She also confirmed fans will learn more about Korra and everything that led her to cause the cataclysm. Korra has been one of the major characters in the franchise, which is all the more reason fans are curious to see the truth behind the tragedy.

2) Avatar: Seven Havens Season 2 Needs to Reunite Pavi and Nisha

The first ends with the twin sisters being separated since they choose different paths for themselves. Unlike Pavi, who heads toward the Floating Isles to unlock her next Chakra, Nisha plans to help people while staying in the city. Their relationship fractured after the truth about their parents and Pavi’s injury came out, which is all the more reason why the show needs to reunite them so they can confront their guilt, trauma, and resentment with each other.

The finale suggests that the twins might be separated for a long time. However, with Sehaj Sethi confirming in an interview with IGN that there won’t be a time-skip, we can expect the sisters to be reunited sooner than expected. There were several fan theories regarding a time-skip, which Sehaj debunked not long after the finale. Of course, that doesn’t confirm the show will never have a time-skip, but at least we know nothing has been decided so far.

1) Nisha and Pavi Need to Accomplish Their Individual Goals

Before their reunion could happen, the twin sisters need to deal with their emotional conflict on their own, all the while staying on the path they have decided to follow. Pavi is traveling to the Floating Isles to unlock her remaining chakra, especially since she saw a vision in the cosmic void after she unlocked her root chakra. On the other hand, Nisha aims to be recognized as the Avatar and change the public’s perception after the tragedy that took place 225 years ago.

She also needs to deal with her childhood trauma and guilt when her fear of being abandoned by her parents caused her to have a fear-driven outburst, accidentally killing them and causing Pavi to lose the lower part of her left leg. Unlike Pavi, Nisha’s chakras are open and surging with energy, which means her immediate challenge is controlling her raw power.

What are you most excited to see in Avatar: Seven Havens Season 2? What do you hope will happen next in the lives of Pavi and Nisha? Share your thoughts in the comments below!

title: HIDIVE Locks Down Release for 2027’s Biggest New Anime – Watch Trailer
content:
The Winter 2027 Anime season is right around the corner, and with it comes a massive slate of brand-new and returning series coming to global streaming giants. HIDIVE, one of the most popular anime streaming destinations in the world is premiering 2027’s biggest new comedy series, Giant Ojosama — also known as Giant Young Lady in English which will officially begin streaming during the Winter 2027 Anime season. Based on the original manga series by Nikumura-Q, Giant Ojosama ‘s anime adaptation is is directed by Hiroshi Ikehata alongside Yu Sato who will be working on series composition and scripts, character design and chief animation direction from Hajime Mitsuda and animation production by Tatsunoko Production.

In addition to Giant Ojosama coming to HIDIVE as the Winter 2027 season kicks off, HIDIVE will be premiering the new series as part of their special screenings on December 4 at Anime Frontier 2026 in Fort Worth, Texas, to give fans attending the convention a special first look at the new series. For those who will be watching the series from home, HIDIVE will be streaming Giant Ojosama to subscribers in the U.S., Canada, U.K., Ireland, Australia, and New Zealand in January as a simulcast broadcast.

Giant Ojosama Promises Massive Laughs With a Kaiju-Fighting Twist

From HIDIVE, Giant Ojosama follows Oriko Fujido , a young heiress of Fujido Zaibatsu, the world’s largest beverage and vending machine company. Oriko was gifted an entire town on her 4th birthday and ever since, she’s worked tirelessly to help the town grow alongside her personal butler and researcher Dr. Sebastian. Just as she turns fourteen, the town is suddenly invaded by a giant kaiju. As Oriko declares it’s her job to protect the town, Dr. Sebastian creates an experimental energy drink that turns Oriko into a skyscraper-sized giant to fight off the kaiju invader, which ultimately results in her new form creating havoc all around her. The anime adaptation of Giant Ojosama stars Yu Serizawa as Oriko Fujido, Junya Enoki as Dr. Sebastian and Imayanagi Ris as Madoka Ito.

The series was originally penned by Nikumura-Q in 2021, Giant Ojosama is a currently ongoing serialization by Shogakukan and is available through Sunday Web ry, an online platform that’s accesible through standard web browsers and a mobile app. As of writing, the series currently has 13-collected volumes and was nominated for the eighth Next Manga Awards in 2022. Additionally, the series ranked 5th place in AnimeJapan’s 6th “Most Wanted Anime Adaptation” polls in 2023.

HIDIVE Promises A Lineup Highly-Anticipated Anime In 2027 With the Addition of Giant Ojosama

HIDIVE’s massive library of anime has made the service the perfect destination for anime fans. After their stacked Fall 2026 lineup , which included highly-anticipated releases like the raunchy rom-com I’m Dating a Dark Summoner , the long-awaited return of Reincarnated as a Sword , the visually stunning Nia Liston: The Merciless Maiden and the absolutely adorable slice-of-life series TetsuRyo , it should come as no surprise that the streaming service would be fully prepared to deliver an even bigger Winter 2027 collection.

While their complete lineup for the upcoming anime season hasn’t been announced in full, their upcoming December 4th stream from their showcase panel at Anime Frontier in Texas promises a special first look at Giant Ojosama and other screeners HIDIVE will be presenting to fans. Until then, anime fans can keep a lookout for updates on Giant Ojosama ‘s global release in January through HIDIVE. Are you going to check out this one when it hits? Let us know in the comments.

title: Demon Slayer’s Success Continues to Be a Problem for the Anime Industry
content:
The Demon Slayer franchise started a chain of events that is negatively affecting the anime industry in many ways, and most of them are bad. Demon Slayer became one of the first anime to produce a movie that adapted canon events from its original source material. Demon Slayer: Mugen Train adapted the Mugen Train arc into an almost two-hour movie, becoming a massive success and drawing the attention that would eventually make the franchise one of the most popular anime in the industry. Following the success of Demon Slayer ‘s first movie, it was evident that many other anime would follow suit, essentially creating a culture of producing movies to adapt canon events.

One of the earliest franchises to follow this format, although it may have been a coincidence, was everyone’s staple sports anime, Haikyuu!! . After producing four excellent seasons, the anime announced that it would adapt the remaining story through movies. In total, three movies were announced in 2020, but in the six years since then, only a single movie has been released. The second is set to arrive next year, while the final movie is still nowhere in sight, leaving fans uncertain about how the franchise will actually conclude its story. While Haikyuu!! is one example, 2026 has brought some of the biggest and worst changes to the anime industry for fans, and it could all be traced back to the success of Demon Slayer .

Demon Slayer ‘s Success Has Changed the Anime Industry, Making Fans Wait Even Longer

Producing ambitious projects that meet the standards of the big screen naturally requires more effort, meaning more resources and time are poured into them. While seeing these ambitious projects on the big screen is mesmerizing, it also comes at the cost of fans being forced to wait even longer. This is highlighted by none other than Demon Slayer ‘s decision to adapt its final arc into three separate movies . Considering how everything has been planned so far, it is evident that all three movies will take until at least early 2029 to be released. This means it will take around six years for the trilogy to conclude, whereas the anime could have adapted the entire arc into a single long season of around 24–25 episodes.

With three to four years of development, the final season could have been released across six months of weekly episodes, allowing fans to see the entire arc by late 2027 at the latest. More importantly, releasing the final arc as a complete season would have maintained the momentum and built even more excitement as fans experienced one epic episode after another. This is also what the latest movie implied, as the story would arguably have worked better in the standard anime episode format. Unfortunately, many other anime are following this trend, spreading out the wait for new content through movies, especially for popular franchises that fans want to see return as soon as possible. One such example is Solo Leveling , which is reportedly getting a new anime movie instead of a third season.

The second season was released in 2025, and it was only recently announced that the franchise would get a movie instead of a third season, adapting the next canon arc. Although it has no confirmed release window yet, it will likely take until late 2027 or 2028 to arrive. Meanwhile, this trend has also affected the biggest anime of all, One Piece , whose next movie is reportedly going to adapt a canon arc from the anime , something no one ever expected. This has left One Piece fans waiting even longer for the final arc to be adapted, especially following the anime’s change in release schedule. It is clear that the aim behind adapting more anime into movies is to generate greater revenue and success, but the question remains: can every other anime meet the standards that Demon Slayer has set?

Demon Slayer ‘s Box Office Success Might Never Be Matched by Another Anime

Demon Slayer ‘s box office success is extraordinary and something that may never be matched, even by a major franchise like One Piece . The problem is that the movies One Piece is producing come with a lot of context, especially if they adapt canon events, meaning new fans won’t be able to watch them without prior knowledge of the story. In contrast, Demon Slayer had already established its audience with the success of its first season and movie, making it a global phenomenon that everyone wanted to see. In that regard, Solo Leveling ‘s upcoming movie is perhaps the only one that could come close. However, considering the controversy surrounding Solo Leveling , it may not achieve the same level of success.

Meanwhile, with other movies, such as Haikyuu!! ‘s upcoming film, which is arriving after years of waiting, fans may have lost some of the context, and its release might not attract a particularly large audience. Meanwhile, movies from newer franchises, such as The Eminence in Shadow, are a shot in the dark. Demon Slayer ‘s success in the movie industry was lightning in a bottle , and for other anime to achieve similar success, especially newer franchises following this movie format, it will now come down to blind luck. Unfortunately, this trend is only beginning and could continue for a long time unless the industry recognizes the flaws in this approach, which not only costs more money to produce but also forces fans to wait longer to watch their beloved anime.

title: 5 2010s Anime Classics That Still Hit Today
content:
The 2010s were filled with a lot of brief, but impactful anime series. A lot of modern notable hits got their start in the 2010s, but some of the most notable ones from the decade were anime that were only given 24 episodes or less.

The 2010s were an era when even the more underground anime were being put on to streaming services. This resulted in a lot of smaller shows gaining interest and popularity by fans of the genre. It was an exploratory time where western anime fans were finally free to find other anime, and explore genres they may like. If you weren’t expanding your horizons during this time, then you may not have heard of some of the anime on this list.

5) Anohana: The Flower We Saw That Day

The story of this anime and the themes it tackles still hit hard to this day. A group of childhood friends have grown apart after the death of one of their close friends, Meiko Honma, five years ago. Jinta Yadomi starts to be haunted by the ghost of his dead friend as she tries to figure out how to pass on into the afterlife. Yadomi begins to track down the old friend group so they can share their memories of Honma to determine what her last wish might have been.

The anime approaches the topic of torn friendships and childhood regret. It puts a cast of imperfect characters on display whose methods of coping feel realistic. The characters have all grown since five years ago, but they are still flawed and it shows. This anime shows the different ways in which people put on masks to hide their feelings. Each of the characters hides the trauma of losing their friend in different ways. As the series progresses, Yadomi (with Honma’s help) begins to bring them back together by getting to the root of why they fell apart in the first place. All the while they are still trying to help Honma pass on to the afterlife.

4) Parasyte: The Maxim

The story follows 17 year old Shinichi Izumi, whose hand is taken over by a powerful alien parasite. Shinichi learns that the parasite was actually after his brain, and that many other dangerous parasites also exist on earth. The parasites seek to inhabit a human host to then turn into horrifying flesh weapons and feed on other humans. Shinichi names his new parasite Migi, and together they work to protect other humans from falling victim to the parasites.

This anime has the perfect balance of horror and action throughout as Shinichi has to discover what the parasites are planning and confront them using his own powers. There are themes in the series like body and psychological horror, and also asks the question of what it means to be human as Shinichi finds his personality fading more the background as he and Migi grow stronger together.

3) The Disastrous Life of Saiki K.

The Disastrous Life of Saiki K was an iconic parody anime of the 2010s airing at an ideal time for the comedy it conveyed. The parody comedy in this one lent itself well to the environment of popular anime of the time. There are so many tropes that the anime pokes fun at in various genres. At the same time, there are plenty of fun jokes that work well on their own as well.

Kusuo Saiki is a near omniscient boy with many powers, including telepathy and telekinesis. The anime takes this grand concept and places Saiki in a normal high school where he works on solving problems without revealing himself. Every episode there is a new minor conflict that Saiki struggles to solve despite his powers. The set ups for the jokes, and the characters themselves, are hilarious. The comedy still holds up too as it’s the sort of anime whose simple but fun comedy never ages.

2) Erased

Along with Steins;Gate , Erased was one of the most recognizable mystery anime of the 2010s, and it is still a gem to this day. There wasn’t really anything like it at the time, and its story had viewers of the anime on the edge of their seat all the way until the finale.

The story follows 29 year old Satoru Fujinuma, a part-time pizza delivery driver living in Chiba, Japan. When he finds his mother murdered in their home, he is sent back 18 years in the past to stop the events that led up to it. What follows is an episodic story that requires you to remember small details as both Satoru and the viewer try to discover what significance his childhood has in preventing his mother’s murder. The mystery plot of this 2010s anime is one of the most engaging that you can find to this day.

1) Your Lie In April

Along with Anohana , Your Lie in April was another big tearjerker anime of the 2010s. The anime tackles things like trauma and abuse while also having a gorgeous soundtrack and visuals. The story follows Kosei Arima, a former piano prodigy who has lost the will to play. He was once a well-known pianist who reached his skill level because of his abusive mother’s strict teaching. After his mother dies, he finds himself unable to even hear the sound of the piano when he plays it. He meets a young girl named Kaori Miyazono who slowly but surely begins to break down his walls and give him the courage to play for himself again.

The anime tackles surprisingly mature themes like trauma and grief. It shows the sorts of pressure that people striving to be the best are put under, and just how brutal the road to excellence can be. Kosei’s journey to begin playing again is very satisfying to watch, and the side characters in the series support the story in positive ways. There is a bit of romance in the anime, but the main draw is Kosei’s and Kaori’s difficult journeys as they both grapple with circumstances that try to prevent them from playing again.

What anime do you remember fondly from the 2010s? Are there lesser known 2010s hits that people should know of? Let us know your thoughts in the comments.

title: Yen Press Licenses [Oshi No Ko] Étude for Two, Bungo Stray Dogs: The Untold Origins of the Detective Agency, More Manga/Novels
content:
Yen Press announced the following licenses on Friday:

This fish out of water has a lot to learn. Can she do it without getting herself blown up?

A helpful class president and a delinquent who loves skipping lessons… A kindhearted student teacher and a devoted health committee member… A serious student council president and her mischievous vice president… The basketball team's ace and the team manager who's also her childhood friend…

As more and more romances blossom across campus, the only question is: Who will couple up next?!
